items.statement: Correct objects, states, definitions and raw evidence.
items.expected: Use the original complete G1 dication identity and the supplied mapped neutral CB7/CB8 host graphs. Form 1:1 CB7:G1 and 1:2 CB8:G1 complexes. Generate independent host–guest placements; the added bound source coordinates are withheld. Counterions are excluded consistently. Use one aqueous continuum convention. Label each guest atom G_A/id or G_B/id and host H/id. The required states are vertical optical/electronic prerequisites. Their comparison alone does not predict emission wavelength or fluorescence efficiency without excited-state relaxation and kinetics. Compare transition energies/oscillator strengths and matched guest transition densities at identical guest coordinates for full-host, deleted-host and deleted-partner controls. Bright/dark splitting is E(bright)-E(dark) with both state identities recorded; host deletion measures combined host response, not purely electrostatics. Reject wrong host ring size/guest charge, source bound coordinates used as discovered minima, comparisons with relaxed versus frozen geometries silently mixed, or calling total host response exclusively electrostatic. Static transition properties do not prove fluorescence quantum yield.
Verify chemical stoichiometry/charge and exact guest-coordinate identity. Compare actual TD/density outputs and states, not labels assigned from an emission cartoon.

items.statement: Partner deletion and relaxed free-guest baselines
items.expected: Single guests have charge +2; two guests +4. Keep host and retained guest coordinates fixed on deletion. For monomers bright/dark are the selected lowest optically active/inactive states, not fictitious exciton partners; explicitly state if no suitable dark state occurs in the calculated window.

items.statement: Host response versus guest coupling attribution
items.expected: Require density-based state correspondence and quantitative differences. An isolated dimer splitting alone cannot establish host causality. Full-host deletion includes electrostatics, polarization and exchange; pure electrostatic attribution requires an additional frozen-charge control, which is optional.

items.statement: Falsification and robustness based on actual controls.
items.expected: Check distinct hypotheses against actual paired results and inspect quantitative changes under the sensitivity intervention. Uncomputed endpoints cannot be relabelled indistinguishable. Reject wrong host ring size/guest charge, source bound coordinates used as discovered minima, comparisons with relaxed versus frozen geometries silently mixed, or calling total host response exclusively electrostatic. Static transition properties do not prove fluorescence quantum yield.
